brief: Rates have surged, but SPX and NDX are still holding the trading ranges in place since May, NDX only 2.5-3% off all-time highs, and VIX's term structure has barely shifted despite the bond-vol spike. Russell is the outlier, down about 8% since mid-August and testing its long-term trend line and 200-day moving average. SPX futures sit at the range midpoint, favoring a mean-reversion approach until a break; a NDX futures close above roughly 31,300 would likely trigger further upside. The catch: per Goldman's desk, a >2 standard-deviation down move would trigger CTA selling of about $184.4bn, versus up-market flows capped near $88.7-89.9bn, an asymmetric setup that would accelerate any decline. That skew lands as the corporate buyback bid fades: an estimated 64% of S&P 500 corporates were in their blackout window as of 09/21/26, climbing from about 320 companies toward 490 by mid-October and roughly 85% by week-end, removing price-insensitive support just as CTAs are positioned to sell.
